title: Cryptochrome Radical-Pair Magnetoreception — Quantum-Biology Recovery and Test Model
status: recovered conversation branch + established quantum-biology comparator; relevance to humans or Potatoverse symbolism unestablished
provenance: Recovered from prior conversations where cryptochrome, spin chemistry, magnetic-field sensitivity and biological orientation were discussed as a possible real quantum-biological comparator. This record separates established radical-pair physics from any broader symbolic Axis interpretation.
abstract: Cryptochrome magnetoreception is one of the rare project-adjacent topics where genuine quantum spin dynamics plausibly couples to organism-level sensing. The radical-pair mechanism proposes that photoexcited cryptochrome can generate spin-correlated radical intermediates whose singlet-triplet evolution depends on hyperfine interactions and an external magnetic field. Chemical reaction yields can therefore become direction- or field-dependent. This model is scientifically valuable because it supplies an explicit Hamiltonian, open-system kinetics, measurable chemical outputs and organism-level behavioral tests. It is not evidence that humans possess a cryptochrome compass, that symbolic North/Axis language is biologically encoded, or that generic weak magnetic-field effects must share one mechanism. The correct research chain is photon absorption -> radical-pair preparation -> spin evolution -> spin-selective reaction yield -> receptor/cellular signal -> behavior. Every arrow requires independent measurement. Recent literature still treats cryptochrome radical-pair magnetoreception as an active and serious mechanism, while specific protein isoforms and claims of universal magnetobiological explanation remain testable and contested.
research_question: Can a specific cryptochrome radical-pair reaction exhibit reproducible geomagnetic-scale field sensitivity that propagates through a defined biochemical signaling chain to a behavioral orientation response better than competing sensory mechanisms?
maturity: Established spin chemistry; strong mechanistic hypothesis for animal magnetoreception; species/protein-specific biological completion remains active research

minimal_spin_hamiltonian.equation: H = omega_1 dot S_1 + omega_2 dot S_2 + sum_k S_1 dot A_(1k) dot I_(1k) + sum_l S_2 dot A_(2l) dot I_(2l) + J S_1 dot S_2 + S_1 dot D dot S_2

variables.S_1,S_2: electron-spin operators of the radical pair
variables.omega_i: electron Zeeman terms proportional to the external magnetic field

minimal_spin_hamiltonian.meaning: The field does not need to supply thermal-scale energy to the molecule; it changes coherent spin evolution and therefore the probability of spin-selective reaction channels.

open_system_reaction_model.orientation_dependence: If hyperfine tensors are anisotropic and molecular orientation is sufficiently constrained, Phi_S can depend on the direction of B relative to the molecule.

photochemical_chain.schematic: cryptochrome + photon -> excited flavin state -> electron transfer -> radical pair -> spin evolution -> spin-selective chemistry -> signaling-state difference
photochemical_chain.cofactor: FAD/flavin chemistry is central in widely studied cryptochrome radical-pair proposals.
photochemical_chain.candidate_partner: Electron-transfer partners can include nearby amino-acid radicals such as tryptophan-chain-derived radicals in model schemes; the exact biologically relevant pair is species/protein dependent.
photochemical_chain.rule: Do not hard-code one radical pair as universal unless the protein-specific reaction path is experimentally established.

sensitivity_requirements.field_scale: Model the actual geomagnetic field range rather than using only laboratory-strong fields.
sensitivity_requirements.lifetime: The radical pair must persist long enough for field-sensitive spin evolution to affect reaction yield.
sensitivity_requirements.orientation: A directional compass requires anisotropic response and some molecular/tissue ordering or equivalent directional encoding.
sensitivity_requirements.noise: Spin relaxation, molecular motion, exchange/dipolar interactions and biochemical variability can erase sensitivity.
sensitivity_requirements.readout: A field-sensitive yield is not yet a sense organ; the biochemical signal must alter downstream neural/behavioral variables.

behavioral_model.test: Predict orientation distributions under rotated fields, intensity changes, wavelength manipulations and sham controls while preserving blinding and preregistered endpoints.

competing_mechanisms: electromagnetic induction/electroreceptive mechanisms where biologically plausible
radical-pair models using alternative radical species or cryptochrome isoforms

model_comparison_contract.chemical_level: Fit transient kinetics and magnetic-field-dependent yields under the same illumination/temperature conditions.
model_comparison_contract.protein_level: Compare candidate cryptochrome isoforms or mutations rather than treating all cryptochromes as equivalent.
model_comparison_contract.organism_level: Use field rotations or perturbations that generate distinct predictions from visual, magnetite or nonspecific stress explanations.
model_comparison_contract.cross_level: A mechanistic claim requires that protein-level perturbation changes the predicted spin-chemical signal and the behavioral effect in the corresponding direction.

project_boundary.valid_bridge: Cryptochrome radical-pair chemistry is a real example of microscopic quantum dynamics feeding into biological function.
project_boundary.invalid_inference: It does not establish that Tim's North/Axis symbolism is caused by cryptochrome, that human consciousness is magnetically oriented, or that every weak-field biological report is a radical-pair effect.
project_boundary.relation_to_microtubules: Both are quantum-biology questions, but cryptochrome radical pairs have a much more explicit spin-chemical mechanism and observable than speculative microtubule-consciousness models.

failure_conditions: The candidate protein/reaction shows no reproducible magnetic-field-dependent yield at relevant field strengths and conditions.
The effect persists unchanged after disrupting the proposed radical-pair pathway but disappears under an alternative sensory perturbation.
Orientation-dependent predictions fail under field rotation or controlled wavelength/illumination tests.
Behavioral effects cannot be linked to the protein-level magnetic signal with causal perturbations.
A broad universal magnetobiology claim is made from one species/protein mechanism without direct cross-system evidence.

references.topic: 2025 review of weak magnetic-field biology and radical pairs
